problem_summary.summary: Compute the greatest h such that at least h papers each have h or more citations.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: citations, one non-negative citation count per paper. Return the researcher's h-index.

brute_force.explanation: Sort a copy of the citation counts, then check each possible suffix size from largest citation downward until that many papers meet the threshold.
brute_force.correctness_idea: In sorted order, papers from index i onward all have at least citations[i] citations; testing these suffix sizes finds the largest qualifying h.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n log n) — sorting dominates the linear scan.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — the input is copied before sorting.

optimized.explanation: Count papers in buckets 0 through n, placing every citation count greater than n into bucket n. Then accumulate counts from n downward; the first threshold h with at least h papers is the answer.
optimized.correctness_idea: The h-index cannot exceed the number of papers. Capping larger citation values at n preserves every comparison relevant to a possible h, while the descending cumulative count gives exactly the number of papers with at least h citations.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — one pass builds buckets and one pass checks thresholds.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary — n + 1 citation buckets are used.
